narrative:
The model estimated a 64% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Although this is not a certainty, it is above the risk threshold used for admission, so your application was denied.

The strongest reason was your part-time enrollment status. Most admitted students were full-time (92.8%), and studying part-time was the single largest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. The second most influential factor was your third-year class standing: your third-year decile of 7 is better than the admitted-student average of 5.79, so this was the one top factor that pushed toward passing and suggests improving later performance. However, it was not enough to outweigh the other signals. The third factor was your first-year class standing: a first-year decile of 4 is below the admitted-student average of 6, which pushed toward failure. Together, these academic-history signals outweighed the positive later-standing evidence.

To improve your position, focus on reducing the risk that part-time study will limit bar preparation. Consider switching to full-time study or documenting a concrete plan to reduce work hours during bar prep. You should also provide evidence of your upward trajectory, such as strong upper-level grades and a detailed study plan, and ask an advisor whether a reconsideration or conditional admission pathway is possible.
